plain_text.primary: You already know which books matter. Bookster gets you through them — key ideas, 15 minutes, actually retained. Start free.
plain_text.headline: Read smarter, not longer.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone + benefit hook for Achievers at mid-funnel produces higher-quality install than generic efficiency copy.
plain_text.learning_question: Does HK_Benefit outperform HK_Problem for a rational, ambitious avatar? ↘ diagonal ST_MOFU.

plain_text.visual: Aspirational palette — rich navy or forest green, warm gold accent. Clean desk setup or curated bookshelf. Feels premium.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle outcome static. Identity-upgrade framing. Not "save time" but "become the person who has read the things that matter."
plain_text.primary: The founders, operators, and professionals who stay sharp share one habit: they actually finish the books. Bookster makes that possible. Start free.
plain_text.headline: The reading list of people who stay ahead.
plain_text.hypothesis: Aspirational tone with problem hook creates tension for Achievers — they recognize the problem but feel pulled forward by aspiration.
plain_text.learning_question: Does TN_Aspirational + HK_Problem outperform TN_Rational + HK_Benefit (C1A) for the Achiever avatar?

plain_text.visual: High-contrast. Dark or navy background, white text. App rating visible (4.8★). Bookster logo prominent. CTA implied in layout hierarchy.

plain_text.headline: Most book apps summarize. Bookster teaches.
plain_text.hypothesis: BOFU assertive comparison for solution-aware Achievers converts the comparison shopper with a direct final push.
plain_text.learning_question: Does ST_BOFU + TN_Assertive produce higher CVR for solution-aware Achievers vs MOFU content?

plain_text.visual: Bold, high-contrast. Dark background. Strong typographic hierarchy. Headline IS the visual. Data element (4M users) as graphic stat.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Confrontational but not hostile. Names the gap between aspiration and reality directly. ↙ diagonal PR_DataDriven.
plain_text.primary: It's not going to happen the way you've been trying. 4 million people changed their approach. 15 minutes a day. Start free.
plain_text.headline: You said you'd read more this year.
plain_text.hypothesis: Hardest combination: PAS + Assertive + Problem hook for Achievers. Tests whether maximum directness converts or repels the ambitious professional.
plain_text.learning_question: Is assertive PAS too aggressive for Achievers, or does the directness cut through where softer tones cannot? ↙ diagonal test.

plain_text.visual: Editorial palette — warm cream, deep green accent. Non-fiction books or podcast headphones. Overlay text structured, clean.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. Not a product demo — shows the reader you become. Editorial feel.
plain_text.primary: Most content disappears within 24 hours. Bookster turns 15 minutes into ideas you actually keep. Try it free.
plain_text.headline: You consume a lot. You retain less than you think.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone creates cognitive dissonance for a depth-seeking aspirational avatar — logical framing where they expect emotional.
plain_text.learning_question: Can TN_Rational work for an identity-driven avatar, or does it flatten the message?

plain_text.visual: App screenshot dominant. Real Bookster library: philosophy shelf, economics shelf, history shelf — real titles visible. Headline overlaid above.
plain_text.concept: Product demo static. App library screenshot showing real book titles across philosophy, history, economics. The breadth IS the proof.
plain_text.primary: Bookster covers the books that matter — philosophy, history, economics, business, science. Read or listen. Key ideas retained. Try free today.
plain_text.headline: 1,000 books. 15 minutes each. Actually understand them.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rebuilt product demo with rational tone and problem hook converts deeper-learning audiences who need to see the product before committing. ↘ diagonal.
plain_text.learning_question: Does showing the real product (CN_ProductDemo) outperform lifestyle framing (C2A) for Depth Seekers?

plain_text.visual: Editorial. Rich, warm palette. Bookster library titles from philosophy and history — real, recognizable titles. Feels like a high-quality curated library.
plain_text.concept: Comparison static. Not cost comparison — quality comparison. Bookster vs skimming content and retaining nothing.
plain_text.primary: Over 1,000 titles spanning philosophy, history, economics, and science — condensed into 15-minute reads that hold the actual ideas. Start learning free.
plain_text.headline: Finally understand the books that matter.
plain_text.hypothesis: Aspirational tone with data proof — aspiration provides identity pull while data validates content quality. ↙ diagonal PR_DataDriven.
plain_text.learning_question: Can PR_DataDriven be aspirationally framed? Does data feel credible or cold for an identity-driven audience?

plain_text.visual: Aspirational editorial. Warm, rich palette. Books, knowledge, intellectual environment. Person implied — curious, engaged. No guilt, no missed deadlines.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. PAS reframed: the problem is not failure — it's untapped capability. Aspirational agitation.
plain_text.primary: The ideas in the books you haven't gotten to yet are still waiting. Bookster closes that gap. 15 minutes. Try free.
plain_text.headline: You're capable of understanding more than you've read.
plain_text.hypothesis: Most unexpected combination: PAS + Aspirational + Benefit hook. Tests whether intellectual aspiration can be agitated effectively.
plain_text.learning_question: Can FW_PAS be aspirationally toned? Does agitating a desire (rather than a pain) work as persuasion?

plain_text.visual: Clean, minimal. White background. Typography-forward. Stat overlay: "80% of books go unfinished." Deliberately rational visual register.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Names the behavioral pattern as a logical sequence. Rational register throughout.
plain_text.primary: Most books lose 80% of readers before chapter 3. The format is the problem — not you. Bookster works differently. Try free.
plain_text.headline: You start books. You don't finish them. There's a reason.
plain_text.hypothesis: Rational tone applied to a naturally emotional avatar tests whether logical or empathetic framing is the correct register for C3.
plain_text.learning_question: Does TN_Rational land for Foggy Brain, or does it feel tone-deaf? Key C3 diagnostic.

plain_text.visual: Warm, calm palette — soft cream or warm white. Open book with bookmark stuck in chapter 1. Feels relatable, not clinical.
plain_text.concept: Behavior shift static. Recognition-first creative. Names the experience without naming any condition. PAS + Emotional register.
plain_text.primary: Most people with a stack of unread books aren't lazy — they're stuck with a format that wasn't built for them. 4 million people switched to Bookster. Try it free.
plain_text.headline: You've started that book three times.

plain_text.visual: Softest visual in the matrix. Warm cream background. Person reading comfortably — relaxed, enjoying it. Small Bookster UI inset. Natural light.
plain_text.concept: Lifestyle static. Not comparison, not demo — identity of the learner who found their way in. Warm, inviting, no shame. ↘ diagonal ST_MOFU.

plain_text.headline: Reading that actually fits how you think.

message_pillars.label: Personal story made physical
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Turn a street into the protagonist of the recipient's life story. The gift lands because the place means something — the emotional core of the brand and the source of the account's best purchase-per-dollar signal.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Pillar ads ('1 Print Static', '2 Print Static', '2 Print + Dads Gift'): $141.69 spend, 4,254 impressions, 1 of 2 account purchases. The converting ad alone: $107.24, 3,160 impressions, CPA $107.24 — vs $364.86 / 0 purchases on the discount grid. Validation_required (single purchase, mixed attribution).
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU cold gift seekers; occasion overlays (Father's Day, anniversary, housewarming) are cycle-2 extensions of this pillar.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Static, warm lifestyle photography, single print staged in a domestic scene, precisely-named street visible in the artwork, short copy (2-4 lines), recipient-reaction narrative, implicit personalization CTA ('Find his city'). Single copy variant per test cell — copy fragmentation (15-29 variants/ad) destroyed isolation in the historical window.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Directional only — conversion-based device export (2026-01-01 → 2026-07-09, wider than the demo window): link clicks skew 94.5% mobile (iphone 932 + android 211 + tablets 83 of 1,298); Feed carries 941 link clicks; the account's single tracked-checkout purchase path ran through Instagram Stories. No placement spend/impressions exist under conversion tracking, so no placement CPA/CTR — run broad placements; treat these splits as delivery hints, not performance reads.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Scale-test candidate per analysis_core, but nothing scales from this window: validate through MST cycle 1 (gift-moment 3x3) first. No cell above 5% of budget for unproven variants.

message_pillars.label: Gallery quality, not a poster
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Neutralize the 'is this just a cheap poster?' objection with spec proof: heavyweight fine-art paper, archival inks, real wood frames, guarantee.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: 'Good quality ad' (retargeting): $127.33, 3,286 impressions, 0 purchases. Analysis_core flags the retargeting pool size as unverified — the read is 'optimize after pool-size check', not 'failed'. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: BOFU retargeting — objection rebuttal for browsers who didn't buy.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Macro product close-up (frame corner, paper texture), 'not a poster' spec language, guarantee + free shipping reassurance, dark-macro design system.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: 25% of budget to BOFU quality-rebuttal retargeting AFTER the pool-size check, per budget guidance. Do not scale prospecting with this pillar.

message_pillars.label: 3,000 cities, breadth and choice
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Any place that matters is printable — hometown, college town, honeymoon coast. Breadth is the rational proof that the buyer's specific place exists in the catalog.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Pillar splits cleanly in the data: authentic spread ('Multiple Pieces' + '6 Images') $255.03, 15,174 impressions, 1 purchase (CPA $172.38 on the converting ad) — while the 25%-off catalog grid ('9 Image + Discount') burned $364.86 / 11,797 impressions / 0 purchases. Breadth converts when proven authentically, not via discount overlay. Validation_required.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU/MOFU solution-aware browsers; the authentic-spread execution carries the pillar, the discount-grid execution is quarantined.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Real (non-mockup) photo of 5-9 framed prints leaned on furniture, catalog-breadth copy ('cities, coasts, and countries'), craftsmanship cues ('museum-quality paper'), NO discount overlay.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Part of the 60% validate allocation: A/B real-photo spread vs catalog-grid mockup at equal budget, no discount in either arm. Hold discount executions at ≤15% of budget pending attribution reconciliation.

message_pillars.label: City identity pride

message_pillars.why_it_matters: 'Music Row Static - Pride' $233.55 / 6,476 impressions and 'Blue Shirt UGC' $53.73 / 1,102 impressions — $287.28 combined, 0 reported purchases across static and UGC formats. Untested geo-tight; do not judge the concept on broad delivery. Validation_required.

message_pillars.execution_specifications: One city per creative, neighborhood name-stack ('Music Row. Lower Broad. East Nash.'), local-identity call-out headline, lifestyle mockup or UGC talking-head format.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Unknown — placement metrics unavailable in this window.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Zero MST-cycle-1 budget. Geo-tight Nashville re-test as a separate experiment before any further spend against this pillar.

campaign_summary.data_caveat: Totals cover the full imported window 2026-03-01 → 2026-07-13.

conversion_tracking_signal.note: Conversion-based tracking: funnel actions are attributed to the converting device/platform/placement. Spend and impressions are not device-attributable under this tracking, so no CPA/CTR exist here. The export window may differ from the account's campaign window — treat cross-surface comparisons as directional.

message_pillars.label: Feed-First Conversion Driver
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Capitalise on Feed placements' dominant share of adds-to-cart and checkout initiations across all device types. Feed rows account for the overwhelming majority of funnel depth signals in the data (e.g., Feed placement rows show 26, 19, 21, 15, 12, 8 adds-to-cart vs. single digits for Stories/Reels). Anchor the matrix's highest-confidence concept columns in Feed-optimised creative formats that maximise thumbstop and carry the user through intent milestones.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Feed placements drove the bulk of conversion-adjacent activity: top Feed rows recorded 26, 21, 19, 15, 12 adds-to-cart and checkout initiations of 6, 7, 5, 5 respectively. The sole confirmed purchase in the placement data also occurred on a Feed row (7 link_clicks, 8 adds_to_cart, 1 purchase). Instagram Stories, Reels, and Facebook Reels each show 1–5 adds-to-cart per row and ≤2 checkout initiations. No purchase is attributed to non-Feed placements. C3 has the lowest CPA (€11.04) and highest CVR (21.6%), suggesting its creative/format approach is best converting within Feed.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU–BOFU: creatives assume problem-awareness and move user from consideration to checkout. Feed format allows copy depth, multi-image carousels, or video with clear CTA.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Optimise aspect ratios for Feed (1:1 or 4:5). Lead with a benefit hook in the first 3 seconds/frames. Include explicit price or value anchor. CTA family: 'Shop Now' / 'See Why X People Chose skov'. Advantage+ placements ON — let the algorithm weight Feed where signals are strongest, but do not exclude other placements to preserve learning.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Run under Advantage+ auto-placements (broad, ABO). Feed will self-select as primary delivery based on historical conversion signals. Do not manually pin to Feed-only — allow Stories/Reels to receive impressions and observe if CVR pattern persists.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Once a Feed-optimised cell wins on CTR/thumbstop signal within 3–5 days and ≥500 impressions, flag for budget reallocation to that ABO ad set. C3's CPA (€11.04) is the current benchmark floor; target ≤€11 CPA at scale before duplicating.

message_pillars.label: C3 Concept Expansion — Low-CPA Angle Scaling
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: C3 is the highest-efficiency concept in the account (CPA €11.04, CVR 21.6% link-click-to-result) despite the lowest spend (€88.29) and only 8 results. The priority is to stress-test whether C3's angle holds at higher spend and across varied tone/hook combinations, before declaring it a scaling winner. This pillar dedicates one matrix column to C3-derivative creatives and systematically rotates the angle variables to isolate what is driving efficiency.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: C3: spend €88.29, 8 results, CPA €11.04, CVR 21.6%. C1: spend €140.61, 9 results, CPA €15.62, CVR 2.8%. C2: spend €414.48, 17 results, CPA €24.38, CVR 6.5%. C3 is 55% cheaper per result than C1 and 55% cheaper than C2, on less than a quarter of C2's spend. Confidence in C3 is currently low due to small volume (8 results); this pillar is designed to build that confidence or falsify it.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU–MOFU: replicate the C3 angle at broader reach to test if CVR holds when impressions scale. Use value-stack and before/after framing to attract cold traffic that mirrors whoever responded to C3.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Keep the C3 concept constant (same design system, same CTA family) across all four cells in its matrix column. Vary FW_ and TN_ across rows A–D. Monitor whether ATC rate stays above the account average as spend crosses €150.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Broad targeting, ABO, Advantage+ auto-placements. Do not restrict audience — the goal is to see if the C3 concept self-selects a winning audience segment organically.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: If C3-column cells sustain CPA ≤€13 after 15+ results, escalate budget 20% every 48 hours. If CPA drifts above €18 (C1 benchmark), pause and revert. Low confidence warning: 8 results is insufficient for statistical certainty; treat early scaling as a hypothesis, not a confirmed winner.

message_pillars.label: iPhone Checkout-Gap Bridge
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: iPhone is the dominant link-click device but shows a disproportionate gap between adds-to-cart and purchases. Across iPhone rows, adds-to-cart total 72 and checkouts initiated total 20 against only 1 purchase. This signals a checkout abandonment or friction problem specific to the mobile-Safari / iPhone experience. A dedicated creative pillar targets this gap with BOFU messaging that reduces hesitation and drives the final conversion step.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: iPhone rows: 11+27+18+7+19+10+30+12 = 134 link_clicks; adds_to_cart: 5+8+16+4+3+12+17+7 = 72; checkouts_initiated: 2+2+4+1+2+2+5+2 = 20; purchases: 1 (only from the row with 10 link_clicks, 12 ATC, 2 checkouts). ATC-to-checkout rate on iPhone ≈ 28% (20/72). The single purchase row has ATC:link_click ratio of 1.2 — unusually high, suggesting that when intent is very strong on iPhone, conversion does close. iPad and Android also show similar checkout drop-off patterns but at lower volume.
message_pillars.funnel_application: BOFU: assume the viewer has already considered the product. Address final objections (risk, trust, delivery, returns). Urgency and social proof are the primary levers at this stage.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Creative should surface trust signals prominently: reviews, guarantees, easy returns, delivery promise. Copy framework: PAS — Problem (still haven't ordered?), Agitate (every day without it is X), Solution (here's why 500+ customers clicked buy). CTA: 'Complete Your Order' or 'Get Yours Today'. Keep creative concise — 15s video or single static with bold social-proof overlay. Note: this pillar assumes checkout friction is partly a creative/messaging problem; a parallel UX audit of the mobile checkout flow is recommended.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements, broad ABO. The algorithm will find recent site visitors and ATC non-converters if the pixel has sufficient data. Do not create manual retargeting audiences — rely on Advantage+ audience expansion to surface high-intent users.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Primary success signal is checkout-to-purchase rate, not CTR. Requires purchase volume to evaluate — do not call a winner until ≥5 purchases per cell variant. Low confidence warning: only 1 purchase is attributed in the entire dataset; purchase-level CPA analysis is not yet viable.

message_pillars.label: Exploratory Avatar Expansion — Instagram-Native Engagement
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Instagram platform rows show consistently competitive ATC rates relative to link clicks (e.g., 8 link_clicks → 5 ATC; 10 link_clicks → 4 ATC; 10 link_clicks → 15 ATC; 1 confirmed purchase on Instagram). However, no established ICP profile is available. This exploratory pillar tests a psychographic/behavioural avatar hypothesis — a visually-driven, mobile-first discovery shopper — using Instagram-native formats (Reels, Stories) to see if a distinct high-intent segment emerges separate from the Facebook Feed audience.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Instagram platform rows: purchases = 1 (8 link_clicks, 8 ATC, 1 purchase — 12.5% link-to-purchase rate, the highest in the dataset). Instagram rows also show ATC:link_click ratios of 0.63, 0.40, 1.50 (the 10/15 row), suggesting some Instagram contexts convert to ATC at rates exceeding Facebook. Facebook has higher absolute volume but Instagram shows at least one outlier efficiency point. All claims are low-confidence due to small sample size and absence of spend/impression data at the platform level.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU: cold discovery. Instagram-native UGC or creator-style video to stop the scroll for an audience with no prior brand exposure. The StoryBrand framework creates character identification quickly.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: 9:16 vertical video, 15–30 seconds, UGC aesthetic (no high-production polish). Hook in first 2 seconds must address a recognisable lifestyle moment. No hard sell — end with a soft CTA ('See how it works' / 'Find yours'). Mark this column clearly as EXPLORATORY in the matrix; avatar_basis is hypothesis only, no historical ICP data to validate.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements. The algorithm will route vertical video to Reels and Stories. Broad targeting — do not add interest or demographic constraints. Watch thumbstop rate and 3-second view rate as primary early signals before any purchase signal is available.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: This is an exploratory column. Do not scale based on ATC alone. Require ≥3 purchases or a CTR significantly above account average before increasing budget. Treat results as directional input for the next MST cycle's ICP definition.

active_hypotheses.label: Replacing a rational benefit-led hook (HK_Benefit) with a social-proof hook (HK_SocialProof) in Feed-optimised creatives will increase adds-to-cart rate, because the dataset's highest ATC:click rows correlate with contexts where trust/validation signals are prominent.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 1 — Feed-First Conversion Driver (CN_ProductDemo + HK_Benefit baseline)
active_hypotheses.risk: Social-proof hooks require credible, specific proof assets (real reviews, real numbers). If proof copy is generic, the hook loses its advantage. Also, small purchase volume means CPA comparison will not be statistically valid within a single sprint.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Swap HK_Benefit for HK_SocialProof across row B of the matrix (cells C1B, C2B, C3B, C4B), keeping all column constants (ICP/design/CTA) and FW_ fixed within each column. Row A retains HK_Benefit as the control row.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: HK_ (Hook type): HK_Benefit (row A, 4 cells) vs HK_SocialProof (row B, 4 cells). Each hook type appears exactly 4 times across 4 different concept columns — meeting the 2–4 distribution rule and spanning all avatars for maximum-confidence isolation. No other row variable changes between rows A and B.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: HK_SocialProof row (B) achieves an ATC rate (adds_to_cart / link_clicks) at least 20% higher than HK_Benefit row (A) after each cell accumulates ≥50 link clicks. Secondary: checkout initiation rate ≥15% higher in row B.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium-high. The dataset shows ATC:click ratios vary widely (0.1 to 1.5+), suggesting hook quality is a significant lever. Social proof is a well-established conversion catalyst at MOFU stage.

active_hypotheses.label: Using a Before-After-Bridge (FW_BAB) copy framework instead of Features-Advantages-Benefits (FW_FAB) in the C3 concept column will sustain or improve CPA below €13 at higher spend, revealing whether C3's efficiency is framework-driven or concept-driven.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 2 — C3 Concept Expansion row A (FW_FAB baseline, CPA reference €11.04 from historical C3 data)
active_hypotheses.risk: Low result volume on C3 historically (8 total results) means the sprint may not generate enough purchase signals for CPA comparison. ATC rate will serve as the proxy metric. Risk of false positive if the C3 concept itself (not the framework) is the primary efficiency driver.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row A of the C3 column uses FW_FAB (control). Row C of the C3 column uses FW_BAB. All other column constants remain identical (same design system, same CTA, same concept angle). Rows B and D of the C3 column use FW_PAS and FW_Direct respectively — giving 4 distinct framework tests within one column.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: FW_ (Copy framework): FW_FAB appears in C3A; FW_BAB appears in C3C. To satisfy distribution rules, FW_BAB also appears in one cell of another column (e.g., C1C) under a different ICP — so FW_BAB appears in 2 cells total across the matrix in different contexts, making it readable. FW_FAB similarly appears in 2 cells minimum.
active_hypotheses.success_criteria: FW_BAB cell (C3C) achieves CPA ≤€13 after ≥5 results, and ATC rate within 10% of the C3A FW_FAB cell. If FW_BAB underperforms by >30% on ATC rate, flag FW_FAB as the framework driver of C3's historical efficiency.
active_hypotheses.expected_impact: Medium. If FW_BAB matches or beats FW_FAB, it unlocks a replicable narrative structure across other concept columns. If it underperforms, it isolates the framework as a variable and directs future testing toward FAB refinement.

active_hypotheses.label: Applying TN_Urgent tonality in BOFU creatives targeting the iPhone checkout gap will increase checkout-to-implied-purchase rate compared to TN_Rational tonality, by reducing deliberation time at the final decision stage.
active_hypotheses.source: Pillar 3 — iPhone Checkout-Gap Bridge (TN_Rational baseline in row C)
active_hypotheses.risk: Urgency messaging can feel manipulative if not grounded in a real reason (limited stock, time-bound offer). If urgency is artificial, it may increase checkout abandonment rather than reduce it. Ensure urgency claims are truthful. Additionally, the dataset has only 1 confirmed purchase — CPA-level validation will require extended run time beyond one sprint.
active_hypotheses.test_variant: Row C across all 4 columns uses TN_Rational (control). Row D across all 4 columns uses TN_Urgent. Both rows share ST_BOFU and AW_MostAware as fixed row constants — only TN_ changes between rows C and D. Each tonality appears 4 times across 4 different concept columns.
active_hypotheses.isolated_variable: TN_ (Tonality): TN_Rational (row C, 4 cells) vs TN_Urgent (row D, 4 cells). Distributed exactly 4 times each — within the 2–4 rule. All other angle variables (FW_, HK_, ST_, AW_, HP_, PR_) remain constant within each column and consistent across rows C and D.

message_pillars.label: Feed-First Product Desire Loop
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Feed placements dominate both click and cart volume across devices. This pillar locks Feed as the primary creative canvas and tests concept angles that maximize thumb-stop and add-to-cart rate — the two most readable early signals available in this account.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Feed placements account for the majority of adds-to-cart in the dataset; the single highest-volume Feed row shows 22 link_clicks → 49 adds_to_cart (ATC rate >200% of clicks, indicating browse/scroll re-exposure), and a separate Feed row delivers 34 link_clicks → 14 ATC. Confirmed purchases on Feed: at least 1 attributed. Instagram Stories shows a strong outlier (2 link_clicks → 16 ATC → 5 checkouts → 1 purchase), suggesting high-intent micro-placement worth isolating. Facebook Reels and Threads each show 1 row with minimal volume — insufficient to action. Evidence is low-volume; treat as directional.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU awareness and ATC generation. Feed creative must earn the scroll-stop AND the cart tap in a single exposure. Stories variant acts as a MOFU retargeting complement.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Square/vertical 4:5 ratio optimised for Feed. Hero visual leads with the pet product in use (lifestyle moment). FAB copy structure: Feature → Advantage → Benefit in three text beats. CTA family: 'Shop Now' / 'See It In Action'. Distinct from Stories variant (9:16, shorter copy). Do NOT produce near-duplicate sizing — treat Feed and Stories as separate concept columns in the matrix.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements ON under Andromeda ABO structure. The Feed-dominant signal supports letting the algorithm allocate, but creative must be natively built for Feed first. Stories-specific creative isolated in its own matrix column so placement signal can be read separately.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Monitor ATC rate (adds_to_cart / link_clicks) as primary thumbstop proxy given purchase volume is too low for CPA verdict at this stage. Scale budget on cells where ATC rate exceeds account average once 50+ ATC events are logged per cell.

message_pillars.label: iPhone-Native UGC Social Proof Engine
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: iPhone is the dominant device across every funnel stage in the dataset. UGC-style creative natively matches iPhone consumption patterns and pairs with social proof messaging to reduce purchase friction — critical given the high checkout drop-off observed (many rows show 5–17 checkouts initiated with 0 confirmed purchases).
message_pillars.why_it_matters: iPhone rows account for 11 of 20 device-level rows. One iPhone row shows 17 link_clicks → 50 ATC → 17 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 11 link_clicks → 55 ATC → 11 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 18 link_clicks → 8 ATC → 8 checkouts → 1 purchase. Checkout-to-purchase conversion is extremely low across all rows (typically 1 purchase per 3–17 checkouts initiated), pointing to a confidence or trust gap at the final step. Android shows weaker ATC ratios. iPad rows are small-sample but show 2 of 3 confirmed purchases — noted but insufficient to action. All purchase counts are low; confidence is limited.
message_pillars.funnel_application: MOFU trust-building targeting warm audiences and broad cold audiences simultaneously (Andromeda broad). The goal is to close the checkout → purchase gap by injecting peer proof before the final tap.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: Raw-feel vertical video (9:16 and 4:5 cuts) shot on or styled as iPhone footage. Real or real-styled pet owner testimonial as hook. StoryBrand structure: character (pet owner) → problem (product search pain) → guide (SKOV Pet) → success (happy pet). On-screen text captions mandatory for silent autoplay. CTA family: 'Read Reviews' / 'See Why Pet Owners Love It' / 'Shop with Confidence'.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements. UGC format performs natively across Feed and Stories without manual placement forcing. Let algorithm route; measure ATC and checkout rate by placement post-hoc.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Track checkout initiation rate (checkouts / ATC) as the key mid-funnel metric. If UGC cells lift checkout rate vs. non-UGC cells by >20% at 30+ checkout events, prioritise budget shift. Do not declare winner on purchase count alone given current low volume.

message_pillars.label: Instagram-First Visual Desire Hook
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Instagram (Feed + Stories combined) carries the highest concentration of ATC events and all but one confirmed purchase in the platform-level data. This pillar tests visually-led, emotion-first angles optimised for Instagram's algorithmic content environment under broad Advantage+ targeting.
message_pillars.why_it_matters: Instagram platform rows: one row shows 17 link_clicks → 42 ATC → 15 checkouts → 1 purchase; another shows 7 link_clicks → 51 ATC → 10 checkouts → 1 purchase; Instagram Stories row shows 2 link_clicks → 16 ATC → 5 checkouts → 1 purchase. Facebook Feed rows by comparison show higher link_clicks but lower ATC ratios (e.g. 17 clicks → 8 ATC, 15 clicks → 11 ATC, 13 clicks → 5 ATC). Instagram appears to generate disproportionate ATC per click. All numbers are low-volume; treat as directional signal only.
message_pillars.funnel_application: TOFU cold audience entry via Instagram Feed and Stories. PAS framework surfaces the pet owner pain (problem hook) → agitates the emotional cost → pivots to SKOV Pet as the relief. Lifestyle visual does the stopping; copy closes the emotional loop.
message_pillars.execution_specifications: High-quality lifestyle imagery or short-form video (under 15s) showing pet + owner in aspirational but relatable home moment. Problem statement in first 2 seconds of video or as headline overlay on static. Aspect ratios: 4:5 for Feed, 9:16 for Stories — built separately, not cropped. CTA family: 'Discover the Difference' / 'Shop Now'. No heavy product spec copy — emotion drives the tap.
message_pillars.placement_strategy: Advantage+ auto-placements with creative natively built for Instagram proportions. Facebook will receive creative via auto-placement but Instagram-native assets should be uploaded directly. Monitor platform-level ATC split post-launch.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: Use Instagram ATC rate as the primary 72-hour signal. If Instagram cells sustain ATC/click ratio >2:1 (as seen in top rows), prioritise spend. Pause Facebook-only cells that show <0.5 ATC/click ratio after 500 impressions per cell.

message_pillars.label: Checkout Friction Eliminator — BOFU Confidence Close
message_pillars.plain_descriptor: Exploratory expansion pillar. The account-wide data shows a systemic checkout abandonment pattern: across nearly every device and platform row, checkouts initiated dramatically outnumber purchases. This BOFU pillar is a transparent exploratory hypothesis — no historical creative data exists for it — designed to test direct confidence-removal messaging (guarantee, returns, trust signals) aimed at the abandonment moment.

Across 20 platform rows: similar pattern. This is not a traffic problem; it is a conversion confidence problem. No existing creative data exists for BOFU-specific angles in this account. This column is EXPLORATORY (avatar_basis: exploratory, target_icp: blank). Numbers are attribution-window estimates; treat with caution.

Value stack communicates offer completeness: product + guarantee + support + fast shipping in one frame.

Here's why 1,000+ pet owners chose SKOV' (copy must be grounded in real social proof before launch — do not fabricate numbers in live creative). Trust badges, return policy, and star rating visible. CTA family: 'Complete Your Order' / 'Get It Risk-Free'. This is an exploratory column — all four cells should vary angle variables broadly to discover what resonates before optimising.

Under pure Andromeda broad structure, this column acts as a BOFU signal test within the broad pool — watch checkout-to-purchase rate as the key metric.
message_pillars.scaling_guidance: This is exploratory. Do not scale before seeing at least 10 purchases attributed across the column's cells. Primary early signal: checkout-to-purchase rate improvement vs. account baseline (~6.4%). If any cell reaches >15% checkout-to-purchase rate at 20+ checkout events, escalate to dedicated BOFU sprint.
